content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as a magnesium blood test, may be conducted to monitor your condition and response to treatment. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for detailed storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health requirements. Before using pantoprazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to similar drugs (such as lansoprazole or omeprazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious underlying condition. Proton pump inhibitors, including pantoprazole, may increase the risk of bone fractures, particularly with prolonged use, higher doses, and in older adults. Older adults may also be more susceptible to side effects such as bone loss and fractures. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Pantoprazole passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications require stomach acid for proper absorption, and pantoprazole reduces stomach acid, potentially affecting how well these products work. Additionally, this medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine tests for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or blood tests for specific tumors, potentially leading to false results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
